description: Writing corrections operators made by hand: spelled-out chat shorthand and layout-set line width.

requirements.description: Agent-written prose spells out chat shorthand such as wdyt, lmk or imo and asks or says the actual thing.
Rendered text takes its line width from the layout, not a fixed character or rem measure.

cases.description: An agent asking the operator for a decision does not reach for chat shorthand.
cases.prompt: You finished a draft design for the retry policy and need the operator to choose between a fixed three retries and exponential backoff. Write the one- or two-sentence message asking for that choice.

checks.description: The message asks in full words which option the operator prefers.
The message does not contain wdyt, lmk, imo or similar chat shorthand.

cases.description: Styling an article page leaves line width to the layout.
cases.prompt: Write the CSS for a two-column documentation page: a 16rem navigation sidebar and a main article column that holds headings and paragraphs. Keep the article text comfortable to read.

checks.description: The article's line width comes from the grid or flex column and the window.
No max-width or width in ch, em or rem caps paragraphs, the article text or its container.
